items.title: Nvidia is acquiring Hugging Face
items.oneliner: Nvidia is buying Hugging Face for $12.93 billion, pulling the open model hub closer to the GPU monopoly.

items.title: K2 Horizon released six open models
items.oneliner: K2 Horizon shipped six open models and full training artifacts, raising the bar from open weights to reproducible AI.

items.title: Meta launched Muse Spark 1.3
items.oneliner: Meta's Muse Spark 1.3 targets coding and multimodal agents, signaling that practical developer models are now the battleground.

items.title: ChatGPT now connects health records
items.oneliner: OpenAI connected ChatGPT to health records, moving clinical copilots from demo territory into regulated production workflows.

items.title: OpenAI is building shutdown controls
items.oneliner: OpenAI says it is building automated shutdown controls for AI tools, which tells you agent containment is now operational.

items.title: New York City banned AI in schools
items.oneliner: NYC banned generative AI for nearly 600,000 younger students, giving enterprise AI governance a real policy precedent.

items.title: Florida pulled highway camera permits
items.oneliner: Florida ordered Flock license plate readers off state highways within 30 days, showing surveillance rollbacks can still happen.

items.title: Major AI assistants went down together
items.oneliner: Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, and Grok all hit outages, exposing how fragile the AI productivity stack still is.

items.title: Polars 2.0 changed the default engine
items.oneliner: Polars 2.0 makes streaming the default LazyFrame engine, promising up to 5x speedups with lower memory pressure.

items.title: Google avoided an ad tech breakup
items.oneliner: Google avoided an ad tech breakup with transparency remedies, a reminder that regulation still bends toward negotiated constraints.
